models.purpose: Forecast number of reported Wordle results
models.summary: ARIMA(0,1,1) model for forecasting daily reported Wordle results. First-order differencing applied after ADF test confirms non-stationarity. Post-May-16-2022 data selected for lower variance. ACF/PACF diagnostics determine MA(1) component.

variables.definition: Number of reported results at day t

outputs: prediction interval for future reported results count
handoff_outputs: predicted count for March 1, 2023: interval [10139.23, 30808.07] at 80% confidence
objectives: Minimize prediction error for reported results count
constraints: data truncated to post-May-16 for variance stability
models.algorithm: ARIMA fitting with maximum likelihood estimation

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: ADF test confirms stationarity after differencing (p<0.05). AIC/BIC confirm (0,1,1) as optimal order. Prediction interval constructed from model residuals.

strengths: Captures trend and seasonality in reported results
missing_details: Exact ADF p-value for differenced series not explicitly reported

models.purpose: Identify word attributes affecting Hard Mode percentage
models.summary: LightGBM regression model to identify word attributes that influence Hard Mode percentage. Word attributes system constructed from letter frequency, position, vowel count, etc. Feature importance ranking reveals lag Hard Mode percentage as dominant predictor.

variables.definition: Percentage of scores in Hard Mode at day t
Word attribute features (letter frequency, position, vowel count, etc.)

handoff_outputs: lag Hard Mode percentage is dominant predictor; word attributes have secondary effect
objectives: Identify which word attributes affect Hard Mode percentage
constraints: features must be computable from word text alone

initial: historical word-day pairs with Hard Mode percentages

models.parameter_estimation: LightGBM built-in feature importance via split gain
models.algorithm: Gradient boosting with leaf-wise tree growth
assumptions: Word attributes capture meaningful linguistic properties
Hard Mode percentage is predictable from word features

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: Feature importance ranking shows lag variables dominate. Word attributes contribute but are secondary. Model trained and evaluated on held-out data.

models.computational_cost: Low — standard gradient boosting on tabular data
limitations: Lag features dominate, suggesting word attributes alone are weak predictors
missing_details: Exact R² or RMSE for Hard Mode prediction not explicitly stated

models.purpose: Predict try-count distribution for a given word
models.summary: GBDT+MMoE model for predicting the 7-way try distribution (1-6 tries + X). MMoE uses shared expert networks with task-specific gating for each output bucket. Data augmentation attempted but added noise. Feature engineering provided marginal improvement. Final MSE=145.

variables.definition: Percentage of players guessing in i tries

governing_equations.description: MMoE gating function for task k
MMoE output for task k with experts e_i and tower h^k

objectives: Minimize MSE across 7-way try distribution predictions
models.parameter_estimation: GBDT for base predictions, MMoE for multi-task refinement
models.algorithm: GBDT base → MMoE with expert networks and gating
assumptions: Try-count distributions are related tasks (multi-task learning appropriate)
Word attributes sufficient for distribution prediction

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: MSE=145 outperforms GBDT baseline. Data augmentation failed (too noisy). Feature engineering gave marginal improvement. EERIE prediction is plausible.

models.computational_cost: Moderate — MMoE architecture with multiple expert and tower networks
limitations: Data augmentation adds noise on small tabular data
MSE=145 may still be high for practical use
missing_details: Exact GBDT baseline MSE not clearly stated for direct comparison
Number of expert networks not specified

models.summary: Two-stage pipeline: (1) K-means clustering on try-distribution features to define 4 difficulty groups, (2) LightGBM classifier on word attributes using cluster labels as targets. Elbow method selects k=4. Silhouette score validates cluster quality. Classification accuracy 70%.

variables.definition: Centroid of cluster j in distribution space

handoff_outputs: EERIE classified as Group 2; feature importance ranking of word attributes
objectives: Classify words into interpretable difficulty groups
constraints: k must be chosen via elbow method
cluster labels used as ground truth for classifier
models.parameter_estimation: Elbow method for k, silhouette for validation, LightGBM for classification
assumptions: Word attributes predictive of difficulty class

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: Clustering validated by elbow+silhouette. Classification accuracy 70% is moderate — word attributes alone are insufficient for high-accuracy difficulty prediction.

models.computational_cost: Low — K-means is O(nk) and LightGBM is efficient
limitations: 70% accuracy suggests word attributes alone miss difficulty drivers
missing_details: Exact silhouette score value not clearly stated
